description.en-US: The attempt this line of evidence belongs to.

Which fulfillment item was attempted. Unique within the attempt: one try reports each item once, and a payload naming the same item twice is refused rather than summed, because the two entries could disagree and nothing could say which was right.
How much this try asked the executor for. Fixed when the attempt is created: it is what was requested, and a result that reports a different total is describing something other than what was asked.

How much physically reached the customer. This is the only quantity in the system that increases what a sale has delivered, and it is summed rather than incremented when the fulfillment item is recomputed, so a redelivered result cannot credit the same goods twice.

How much the executor could not hand over. It never reduces what is still owed: goods that failed to come out are still goods the customer paid for, and treating a failure as a delivery is the exact mistake this column exists to prevent. What it does feed is the failure policy, which decides whether to refund, wait, or park the shortfall.

How this item ended, derived from the two quantities rather than asserted by the reporter: everything dispensed is success, nothing is failure, some of each is partial. Derived so a reporter cannot claim success while reporting a shortfall, which would settle a sale that still owes goods.

The executor's own machine-readable reason, such as a jammed slot. Kept unparsed and uninterpreted: Sales decides what a failure COSTS by policy, never by which fault the hardware reported, and a rule keyed on a device code would break with the next firmware.
The human-readable form of the same, for an operator reading a log or a support agent explaining a shortfall to a customer.
